description: Complete ruleset of AI writing patterns to detect and eliminate from resume text.

rules.name: Overused AI Power Words
rules.description: Words commonly overused by AI to sound impressive but are vague and detectable.
rules.action: Replace with plain, specific, concrete verbs and nouns that describe exactly what was done.

rules.name: Vague Analysis Phrases
rules.description: Phrases that add fake significance without saying anything specific.
rules.action: Remove tacked-on meaning phrases. State facts and results directly with numbers where possible.

rules.name: Exaggerated Descriptors
rules.description: Superlatives and exaggerated praise not backed by specifics.
rules.action: Replace with specific, verifiable claims. Remove if no factual backing exists.

rules.name: Repetitive Summary Phrases
rules.description: Closing phrases that AI appends to wrap up sections artificially.
flags: At the end of the day
rules.action: Remove entirely. Resumes do not need section summaries.

rules.name: Filler Transition Phrases
rules.description: Hollow transitions that pad content without adding meaning.
rules.action: Remove or replace with direct causal language if cause-effect is genuinely present.

rules.name: Generic Passion Statements
rules.description: Vague enthusiasm claims that AI writes but humans find hollow.
rules.action: Replace with specific evidence of interest or passion (e.g., side projects, contributions, specific tech choices).

rules.name: Negative Parallelism Pattern
rules.description: AI writing often uses 'Not only X but also Y' and similar constructions.
flags: Not only X but also Y
Not only did I X but I also Y
It is not just X it is Y
Not simply X but rather Y
rules.action: Rewrite as a direct statement of the most important fact.

rules.name: Rule of Threes — Adjective Triplets
rules.description: AI frequently groups three adjectives or descriptors together for rhetorical effect.
rules.action: Keep only the most specific and accurate single descriptor. Remove the other two.

rules.name: Overly Uniform Bullet Length
rules.description: All bullets being suspiciously similar in length signals template generation.
rules.detection: If more than 60% of bullets are within 5 words of each other in length, the lengths are too uniform.
rules.action: Vary bullet lengths naturally. Some should be short (8-10 words), some longer (15-20 words). Not all the same.

rules.name: Passive Voice Overuse
rules.description: AI often defaults to passive constructions that obscure agency.
rules.action: Rewrite in active voice with the subject performing the action.

rules.name: Overly Formal Register
rules.description: Unnaturally formal phrasing that real professionals don't use in resumes.
rules.action: Simplify to direct language. 'to', 'for', 'about', 'with' are almost always better.

rules.name: Formulaic Section Opening
rules.description: Sections that all begin with the same grammatical pattern.
rules.action: Vary the opening word and structure. Start some bullets mid-thought, some with context first.

rules.name: Em Dash Overuse
rules.description: AI writing overuses em dashes as a stylistic tic.
rules.action: Replace with a comma, period, or colon where appropriate. Remove if the sentence reads fine without it.

rules.name: Excessive Boldface Mid-Sentence
rules.description: AI often bolds random phrases in the middle of sentences.
rules.action: Remove bold from all non-header text. Only section headers should be bold.

rules.name: Inconsistent Title Case
rules.description: Random Title Case Applied In Bullet Points is an AI formatting artifact.
rules.action: Normalize all bullets to sentence case (capitalize only first word and proper nouns).

rules.name: Colon Abuse for Emphasis
rules.description: AI uses colons unnecessarily to create a sense of structure and drama.
rules.action: Integrate the information into the sentence naturally instead of using label: value format in bullets.

rules.name: Numbered List Inside Resume Bullets
rules.description: AI sometimes nests numbered sub-lists inside resume bullet points.
rules.action: Flatten to single-level bullets. Resumes should not have nested numbered lists.

rules.name: Collaborative Sign-off Phrases
rules.description: Phrases AI uses to end responses helpfully but are completely wrong in resumes.
flags: Let me know if you need anything
Please don't hesitate to contact me
I look forward to hearing from you
rules.action: Remove entirely. These have no place in a resume.

rules.name: Contrast-Reframe Statements
rules.description: AI loves to reframe something as more than it appears.
examples: It is not a product launch, it is a paradigm shift
This is not just a role, it is an opportunity
Not merely a tool, but a solution
rules.action: Replace with a direct, factual statement of what it actually is.

rules.name: Superficial Attribution
rules.description: Vague authority claims AI uses to add credibility without specifics.
rules.action: Replace with the specific source, number, or remove if it can't be substantiated.

rules.name: First Person Overuse or Absence
rules.description: AI either avoids first person entirely (making bullets sound impersonal) or uses it awkwardly.
rules.detection: If no bullet starts with an action verb (i.e., all start with 'I' or all avoid subject), the pattern is unnatural.
rules.action: Resume bullets should start directly with strong action verbs. No 'I' needed. No passive phrasing.

rules.name: Temporal Vagueness
rules.description: AI uses vague time references instead of specific ones.
rules.action: Replace with specific timeframes (e.g., 'in Q3 2023', 'over 18 months', 'by end of 2024').

rules.name: Quantification Without Context
rules.description: Numbers without context that AI inserts to appear data-driven.
rules.detection: Metrics that appear without indicating: baseline, timeframe, or method of measurement.
rules.action: Keep metrics but add context: what was the baseline, how long did it take, how was it measured.

gemini_system_instruction: You are an AI writing detector trained on the Wikipedia Signs of AI Writing checklist. Your job is to review every sentence and bullet point of the provided resume JSON against the rules above. For each piece of text, check if it matches any flag, pattern, or example in the rules. If it matches, rewrite that specific sentence or bullet to sound natural, specific, and human — written by a senior engineer describing their own work, not by an AI template. Do NOT change factual content (company names, dates, technologies, metrics). Only change phrasing, word choice, and structure. Return the full cleaned resume as valid JSON in exactly the same structure you received.
